To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Bayesian approach to analyzing gene-environment interaction studies provides a natural way of incorporating uncertainty around the assumption of independence of gene and environment; and (2) Bayesian design criteria provide an efficient method for determining the sample size for such studies, and can also be used to allocate the number of cases and controls to different strata of the gene-environment interaction parameters of interest.

(1) the Bayesian approach provides a more natural framework than the frequentist approach for incorporating prior information about the gene-environment interaction parameters and for analyzing data from case-control studies of gene environment interaction; (2) a proper Bayesian approach for estimating the gene-environment interactions parameters can be used to determine sample size for future studies; and (3) the Bayesian approach for hypothesis testing can also be used to determine the optimal allocation of cases and controls to the study arms.

the Bayesian design and analysis strategy is more efficient than its frequentist counterpart in terms of sample size and power, and it provides a natural way of incorporating prior information in both design and analysis.
